# useList

> An array in state with immutable `push`, `insertAt`, `updateAt`, `removeAt`, `move`, `filter`, `clear`, `reset`.

🟡 intermediate · React 16.8+ · Custom Hooks › State utilities · support: universal

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-list`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-list)

## Concept

Every action is a functional `setState` that returns a new array — or the _same_ array when nothing changed, so React bails out of the re-render.

## Problem

Mutating methods (`push`, `splice`, `sort`) change the array in place: React compares state with `Object.is`, sees the same reference and does not re-render.

## When to use

- Editable lists, reorderable items, form field arrays in small UIs.

## When not to use

- Large lists edited deeply — consider `useReducer` with Immer or a normalized store.
- Complex form arrays with validation — use a form library (e.g. React Hook Form `useFieldArray`).

## API

```ts
function useList<T>(initialList?: readonly T[] | (() => readonly T[])): readonly [
  readonly T[],
  {
    set;
    push(...items);
    insertAt(index, item);
    updateAt(index, updater);
    removeAt(index);
    move(from, to);
    filter(predicate);
    clear();
    reset();
  },
];
```

| Parameter                  | Type                                 | Description                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `initialList` _(optional)_ | `readonly T[] \| () => readonly T[]` | Initial items (also used by `reset`). |

**Returns:** `[list, actions]`; the actions object is stable for the component lifetime.

## Common mistakes

### Mutating state in place

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
list.push(item);
setList(list);
```

Same reference → React skips the render, and the previous render's data was mutated too.

✅ Correct:

```tsx
actions.push(item); // setList((previous) => [...previous, item])
```

## Edge cases

- Out-of-range or negative indices are ignored (not counted from the end); `insertAt` clamps.
- `updateAt` returning the same item, `filter` removing nothing and `clear` on an empty list keep the previous array.
- Index-based actions use the index at update time — prefer stable ids for keys.

## Browser support

Uses ES2023 `Array#with`/`toSpliced` (Baseline 2023).

## Testing

Tests check each action, that previous arrays are never mutated, that no-ops keep the same reference and that updates compose.
